method: 45 new records screened and 13 individually scoped official UNESCO site claims checked. Classification is preliminary for all other claims. All 45 are country/territory content records, not necessarily sovereign states.

records.title_en: Brunei: rainforest and north Borneo coast
records.nature_excerpt_en: Features include Ulu Temburong rainforest, coastal wetlands and the stilt-water settlement Kampong Ayer.

records.title_en: Benin: coast, savanna and historic kingdoms
records.nature_excerpt_en: Highlights include Lake Nokoué and coastal fishing habitats, and Pendjari National Park in the northern savanna, where river systems and wildlife habitats meet.

source.site: Pendjari National Park within W-Arly-Pendjari Complex
source.verification_scope: The article identifies Pendjari; UNESCO confirms the complex is transnational Benin/Burkina Faso/Niger

records.title_en: Burkina Faso: savanna and inland plateau
records.nature_excerpt_en: The Sindou area features striking eroded rock formations, while seasonal savanna woodland, valleys and water bodies change between wet and dry periods.

records.title_en: Burundi: highlands and Lake Tanganyika
records.nature_excerpt_en: Lake Tanganyika is a deep freshwater ecosystem with diverse life; Burundi's highlands contain grasslands, remaining montane forests and terraced farming landscapes.

records.title_en: Cabo Verde: volcanic Atlantic islands
records.nature_excerpt_en: Pico do Fogo volcano dominates Fogo, Santo Antão features steep valleys and ridges, and Sal and Boa Vista have sandy beaches and arid coastal landscapes.

records.title_en: Central African Republic: forests, savanna and rivers
records.nature_excerpt_en: The southern Dzanga–Sangha forests protect extensive rainforest habitats, the Ubangi is a prominent river corridor, and northern regions contain savanna ecosystems.

source.verification_scope: Dzanga-Sangha rainforest habitat in Central African Republic; source confirms transboundary property

records.title_en: Chad: Sahara and Lake Chad
records.nature_excerpt_en: The Ennedi Plateau features sandstone arches and ancient rock art, Tibesti has volcanic peaks, and the Lake Chad basin contains wetlands with highly variable seasonal extent.

source.verification_scope: Sandstone arches and rock art in Ennedi mentioned in article

records.title_en: Comoros: volcanic Indian Ocean archipelago
records.nature_excerpt_en: Active Karthala volcano dominates Grande Comore; montane and coastal forests and reefs support varied island habitats.

records.title_en: Republic of the Congo: forests and Congo River
records.nature_excerpt_en: Odzala-Kokoua has swamp forests and natural clearings; Congo Basin rainforests and coastal plains provide habitats for forest elephants and primates.

records.title_en: Djibouti: Gulf of Tadjoura and Lake Assal
records.nature_excerpt_en: Lake Assal, volcanic Afar terrain and reef-lined coasts around the Gulf of Tadjoura form contrasting landscapes under intense heat and scarce rainfall.

records.title_en: Equatorial Guinea: Bioko and mainland forests
records.nature_excerpt_en: Landmarks include Pico Basilé on Bioko and the coastal and inland forests of Río Muni. Humid forests and wetlands provide diverse habitats despite the country's relatively small land area.

records.title_en: Eritrea: Red Sea and highlands
records.nature_excerpt_en: Landscapes include the Asmara highlands and escarpments, reef-fringed Dahlak Islands and dry coastal lowlands. Maritime transport and fishing have long shaped coastal communities.

records.title_en: Eswatini: mountains, grasslands and valleys
records.nature_excerpt_en: The Malolotja highlands protect valleys and upland habitats; Hlane holds savanna ecosystems, while the Ezulwini Valley lies between mountain districts.

records.title_en: Gabon: equatorial forests and Atlantic
records.nature_excerpt_en: Gabon includes Lopé, Ivindo and Loango national parks, spanning rainforests, waterfalls, coasts and wetlands supporting terrestrial and marine wildlife.

source.verification_scope: Both Lopé and Ivindo nature sites are in the article and official country listing

records.title_en: The Gambia: a country along one river
records.nature_excerpt_en: The Gambia River defines the country's landscape through wetlands, mangroves and bird habitats. Natural sites include Abuko Nature Reserve, while Kunta Kinteh Island is a historical landmark associated with the river.

records.title_en: Guinea: headwaters of West Africa
records.nature_excerpt_en: Fouta Djallon holds river headwaters and waterfalls; the Mount Nimba area contains distinct mountain and forest habitats, while islands off Conakry offer coastal ecosystems.

source.verification_scope: Mount Nimba forests and highlands; UNESCO World Heritage property shared Guinea and Côte d'Ivoire, not Liberia

records.title_en: Guinea-Bissau: Bijagós and estuaries
records.nature_excerpt_en: Highlights include the Bijagós Islands, mangroves and bird-rich tidal flats. Bijagós mangroves, mudflats and shallow waters support fish and birds; coastal livelihoods are closely linked to tidal cycles.

records.title_en: Guyana: forests, rivers and Guiana Highlands
records.nature_excerpt_en: Kaieteur Falls plunges along the Potaro River through rainforest and is one of Guyana's best-known natural landmarks. Inland highlands feature rocky plateaus, forests and rivers, while estuaries and wetlands merge with the Atlantic coastal plain.

records.title_en: Liberia: Atlantic tropical forests
records.nature_excerpt_en: Highlights include Sapo National Park, eastern forests and Atlantic beaches. Sapo National Park protects important Liberian rainforest within the Upper Guinean forest ecosystem, which supports diverse wildlife.

records.title_en: Lesotho: the mountain kingdom
records.nature_excerpt_en: The Maloti highlands have alpine grasslands, steep valleys and occasional winter snow; Katse Dam lies among the rugged mountain valleys.

records.title_en: Mali: Niger River, Sahara and Sahel cities
records.nature_excerpt_en: Landmarks include the seasonally flooded Inland Niger Delta, rocky Bandiagara Escarpment and historic Timbuktu and Djenné. Agriculture and livelihoods are closely linked to changing water levels.

records.title_en: Mauritania: Sahara and Atlantic coast
records.nature_excerpt_en: Highlights include coastal Banc d'Arguin, the Richat Structure and Adrar Plateau.

source.verification_scope: Coastal Banc d'Arguin explicitly named in Nature & Landmarks

records.title_en: Niger: Sahara and Niger River
records.nature_excerpt_en: The Aïr Mountains contain rocky peaks, oases and rock art, while the Ténéré has desert plains and dunes. The Niger River supports riparian habitats in the otherwise dry Sahel.

records.title_en: Sierra Leone: Freetown Peninsula and forests
records.nature_excerpt_en: The Freetown Peninsula combines beaches and wooded hills; Tiwai Island contains riverine forest, while the Loma Mountains support distinctive upland wildlife.

records.title_en: Somalia: Horn of Africa and ocean
records.nature_excerpt_en: Coasts span the Gulf of Aden and Indian Ocean with beaches and headlands; the Juba and Shabelle valleys and Cal Madow highlands provide contrasts between marine, mountain and arid environments.

records.title_en: South Sudan: Sudd wetlands and Nile plains
records.nature_excerpt_en: The Sudd is among the largest tropical wetland systems, supporting birds, fish and other wildlife. Flood extent and grassland patterns change seasonally.

records.title_en: Suriname: Guiana forests and estuaries
records.nature_excerpt_en: The Central Suriname Nature Reserve protects an extensive interior rainforest landscape and is a natural World Heritage site. Rivers, rocky outcrops and diverse wildlife characterize the interior, while estuaries and mangroves are important coastal habitats.

source.verification_scope: Primary tropical forest protected within reserve explicitly named

records.title_en: Togo: from Gulf coast to savanna
records.nature_excerpt_en: Highlights include Lake Togo, Kloto Highlands and Fazao-Malfakassa National Park. Central districts include Kloto's upland forests; Lake Togo is associated with coastal lagoons, while northern areas contain savanna habitats.

records.title_en: Andorra: Pyrenean mountain principality
records.nature_excerpt_en: Andorra has small glacial lakes, mountain meadows and pine forests; the Madriu–Perafita–Claror Valley is an important protected cultural landscape.

source.verification_scope: Cultural high-Pyrenean valley named in Nature & Landmarks

records.title_en: Antigua and Barbuda: Caribbean bays and islands
records.nature_excerpt_en: Antigua and Barbuda combines Antigua's bays, beaches and low hills with flatter Barbuda's coastal lagoons and coral habitats. The differences make reefs, mangroves and wetlands important conservation features.

records.title_en: Dominica: island of rivers and volcanoes
records.nature_excerpt_en: Morne Trois Pitons National Park includes Boiling Lake, hot springs and montane forests, with waterfalls and steep valleys across the interior.

source.verification_scope: Boiling Lake and volcanic geothermal features in named park

records.title_en: Grenada: spice island and mountains
records.nature_excerpt_en: The island includes Grand Etang crater lake, mountain forests and Grand Anse beaches, with smaller islands and coral habitats to the south.

records.title_en: Saint Kitts and Nevis: volcanic twin islands
records.nature_excerpt_en: Mount Liamuiga rises on Saint Kitts, while Nevis has volcanic slopes and hot springs; both islands include beaches, reefs and coastal habitats.

records.title_en: Saint Lucia: Pitons and rainforest
records.nature_excerpt_en: Highlights include Gros Piton and Petit Piton, Soufrière springs and coastal bays. Gros Piton and Petit Piton are distinctive volcanic peaks; rainforests and hot springs near Soufrière reflect the island's humid tropical environment.

source.verification_scope: Gros Piton and Petit Piton in current country article

records.title_en: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines: volcano and islands
records.nature_excerpt_en: Highlights include La Soufrière volcano, Tobago Cays reefs and smaller islands such as Bequia and Mustique, combining volcanic landscapes and marine habitats.

records.title_en: Kiribati: atolls and the date line
records.nature_excerpt_en: Highlights include the Phoenix Islands Protected Area and lagoons at Tarawa and Kiritimati.

source.verification_scope: Protected marine site named in Nature & Landmarks; superlative protected area size ranking not treated as current

records.title_en: Maldives: Indian Ocean coral atolls
records.nature_excerpt_en: The Maldives has coral atolls, reef barriers and shallow lagoons, with marine habitats supporting reef fish, turtles and manta rays. Very low island elevations and changing reef health affect exposure to waves and coastal erosion.

records.title_en: Marshall Islands: atolls and vast ocean
records.nature_excerpt_en: The Marshall Islands comprise atolls surrounding broad lagoons, with low sandy islets and reefs supporting fish and seabirds. Freshwater scarcity and exposure to waves are major environmental concerns.

records.title_en: Federated States of Micronesia: four island states
records.nature_excerpt_en: Highlights include Nan Madol ruins on Pohnpei, Chuuk Lagoon and coral islands.

source.verification_scope: Nan Madol ruins on Pohnpei explicitly named

records.title_en: Nauru: phosphate-bearing coral island
records.nature_excerpt_en: The interior plateau contains exposed limestone formations shaped by mining and erosion, while reefs fringe the island and most settlements line the narrow coast.

records.title_en: Palau: marine lakes and Rock Islands
records.nature_excerpt_en: Palau is known for the limestone Rock Islands, their relatively isolated marine lakes and narrow channels, as well as coral reefs and coastal forests. Higher islands differ from low atolls in freshwater and vegetation.

source.verification_scope: Limestone Rock Islands and marine lakes named in Nature & Landmarks

records.title_en: Tuvalu: low atolls of the Pacific
records.nature_excerpt_en: Tuvalu consists of low coral atolls and islands with shallow lagoons and reefs, including Funafuti. Storms, coastal erosion and limited freshwater shape life on its narrow land strips.

records.title_en: San Marino: republic in the Apennines
records.nature_excerpt_en: San Marino combines Apennine hill landscapes, Mount Titano's peaks and historic fortifications, with small rural areas around settlements.

records.title_en: Greenland
records.nature_excerpt_en: Ilulissat Icefjord is renowned for icebergs calving from a major glacier; coastal fjords and uplands support distinctive Arctic habitats.

records.title_en: Faroe Islands
records.nature_excerpt_en: Múlafossur Waterfall, Mykines and sea cliffs. Mykines is known for seabirds and cliffs; Múlafossur descends near the village of Gásadalur.

precautions: UN M49 is a statistical country or area classification, not a sovereignty determination.
No UNESCO-wide country link certifies every claim in an article; records with a source are narrowly scoped.
Crossborder W-Arly-Pendjari, Sangha Trinational and Mount Nimba sites must retain correct multiple-country geography.
Some article titles represent dependencies, nonsovereign islands, or historical codes; those require targeted review.
Do not change UI or photo libraries based on an unverified asset.
